math.targetRTP:
97.0% (published), measured against the OPTIMAL-STOPPER policy, not the average player. Sim confirms peak-stop RTP = 96.97% at the implied sweet spot (L10), confirmed over 400k Monte Carlo, fixed-seed (mulberry32 in probe; production uses SHA-256(serverSeed+clientSeed+nonce)). Every number below is a SIM TARGET, not an assertion — sim.html is the first commit and must reproduce these to ±0.3% before art is built.

STRUCTURAL RESOLUTION OF THE MUST-FIX CONTRADICTIONS (these override the doc's prose where they conflict):
1. EV-monotonicity claim is FALSE and is ABANDONED. The honest pillar is now: "An implied sweet spot exists (~L8–L10); the house edge is baked into the catch/cap/snap distribution and players overstay. Past the peak, bleed + LINE SNAP + escalating EXTEND cost punish greed at a flattening (Σ-capped) ceiling." This is the real Aviator/Spaceman model.
2. THE L6 FREE-BANK EXPLOIT IS KILLED BY CONSUMING THE STAKE. PULL pays ONLY the summed caught-fish multipliers — there is NO stake-return floor. A fishless or thin-school pull is a net loss. Sim: L3 stop = 8.6% RTP, P(0)=31%; you only profit if you actually built a school. There is no zero-downside parking spot because stopping early simply means you spent stake and caught little.
3. THE DOC'S PUBLISHED PER-FISH MULTS ARE INCOMPATIBLE WITH SUMMING+38%-CATCH AT 97% RTP — this is the dominant finding. With summing across ~10 ledges at catch~0.45, the doc's x0.8/x2-6/x8-40 ranges sum to 1000%+. The model KEEPS SUMMING and RESCALES per-fish mults down (effective ~x0.06–x2.8 per fish); the HEADLINE number players see is the SUMMED Σ, not any single fish.
math.volatility: High / crash-class. P(0) ramps 0% (L1–6) → ~15% on a full L12 chase; sub-1× fraction is the majority of all pulls (L3 ~92% sub-1×, sweet-spot L10 ~60% sub-1×). Hit-frequency (>1× net) at the sweet spot = 38–40% (sim: L8 38.4%, L10 39.7%) — the doc's 38% target IS achievable at the implied optimal stop and was NOT relaxed. Variance profile: many small-to-zero outcomes funding a heavy right tail capped at ×500. Tail discipline: top-1% / near-cap (≥×450 of the ×500 cap) RTP contribution is an explicit sim acceptance gate; soft-compression above ×350 (Σ above 35000bp compressed at 0.45 rate) keeps the certifiable tail bounded so CURRENT-injection + GOLDEN SHOAL + summing cannot stack into an uncertifiable spike.
math.betModel: One STAKE per round = base unit B (config-driven, e.g. ₹/R$ 10–10,000 selectable). All internal math in integer basis points: stake B = 10000bp = ×1.00 reference; one fish's mult x0.8 = 80bp. DROP costs 1×B and auto-sinks the free band L1–6, seeding/revealing fish through L6. From L7 each EXTEND tap charges ADDITIONAL stake on top: L7–8 +0.4×B (4000bp), L9–10 +0.8×B, L11–12 +1.5×B — charged only on the tap, only if you tap. Total spend on a full L12 chase = 1.0 + 0.4+0.4 + 0.8+0.8 + 1.5+1.5 = 6.4×B. PAYOUT = B × (Σ of surviving caught-fish mults), capped at ×500 = 50000bp. The bet is the cost of variance: deeper = more accumulated potential but strictly worse marginal EV past the peak (each Deep ledge's marginal contribution is <1× of its EXTEND cost in expectation).
math.depthModel: 12 ledges, 3 bands. Shallows L1–3 / Reef L4–6 / Deep L7–12 (deep shortened to 6 per doc so cumulative SNAP over a full chase stays ~11–15%). L1–6 auto-sink, free, 0.9s/ledge skippable (skip = instant state-resolve to L6, not a fast-forwarded animation — zero animation cost). L7–12 are explicit EXTEND taps with escalating cost above. DEPTH TIERS / escalating risk: (a) EXTEND cost ramps ×0.4→×0.8→×1.5; (b) LINE SNAP P(0) gated by depth — 0% across L1–6, then ramps linearly 1.0%→4.0% across L7→L12 (formula: snap(L)=0.01+(L−7)×0.006 for L≥7); cumulative survival to L12 ≈ 0.99·0.988·0.976·0.964·0.952·0.94 ≈ 84.8%, i.e. ~15% full-chase ruin; (c) BLEED — Deep-only per-fish-per-ledge escape: low-value fish (mult <×20 effective) 2%/ledge, high-value (≥×20) 8%/ledge; erodes already-caught value the longer you hold. Shallows/Reef never bleed and never snap, BUT the consumed-stake payout means there is still no free-EV park there (you simply caught too little to profit). The implied sweet spot is L8–L10 where accumulated Σ peaks before bleed+snap+ext-cost overtake it.

math.pullUpRules: PULL transitions FSM HOLD→PULLING (input-locked). The hook rises; each ALREADY-caught survivor resolves at its pre-tagged state. PAYOUT = B × softcap( Σ over surviving fish of fishMult_i ), in integers, divide only at display. softcap: if Σ ≤ 35000bp → Σ; else 35000 + (Σ−35000)×0.45, hard-clamped at 50000bp (×500). NO stake is returned — the stake (and any EXTEND spend) is fully consumed; payout is purely the summed catch. This is the exploit-killer: stopping early with a thin school is a net LOSS, so no ledge is a zero-downside park. TWO DISTINCT LOSSES preserved: (1) BLEED ESCAPE — before PULL, on each Deep ledge held, each caught fish independently rolls its bleed rate (2% low / 8% high); a bled fish desaturates, shatters, sets mult=0 (shards sink past the rising hook); recoverable dread, single soft chime. (2) LINE SNAP — rolled on ENTERING each Deep ledge (consume order: spawn→mult→catch→bleed→snap), P per ledge = 0.01+(L−7)×0.006; on snap, ALL tags shatter, payout=0, the ONE magenta flash (or per art-director must-fix: gold violently DRAINS to cold-black — temperature axis reversed — rather than imported magenta). Always pre-telegraphed by the pressure column so it never reads as a rug-pull. Escape/dwindle: the longer you hold past L7, the more the accumulated Σ erodes (bleed) AND the higher the next-ledge P(0) — this is the EV-shaping mechanism, gentler than relying on snap alone.
bonusTriggers: NET (~3% per round): auto-catches every fish currently above the hook, bypasses bleed. Mesh (non-fish) geometry per silhouette grammar. One extra consume roll.

CURRENT (~4% per Deep ledge, Deep L7–12 ONLY): flashes one Abyss-class fish (x40–80) into the current ledge — the 'big one' near-miss that fires from the zone players actually reach. +2 RNG rolls (spawn-position + mult). MUST be rate-bounded: at inject rates above ~5% it becomes a catch-independent RTP floor that dominates the optimal-stopper solve and pushes RTP past target (verified in probe — the solver collapsed CATCH→0). Flow-streak (non-fish) geometry.

GOLDEN SHOAL (~1.5% per ledge): spawns 3 fish at once at the current ledge's tier. +3 fish → +up to 12 rolls (spawn,mult,catch,bleed each). This is the primary byte-budget worst case: when CURRENT(+2) and GOLDEN SHOAL(+3 fish) co-occur on one nonce and exhaust the 32-byte SHA-256 output, REHASH with an incrementing counter (SHA-256(serverSeed+clientSeed+nonce+ctr)) as an explicit, unit-tested step in the consume order; worst-case ctr iterations bounded and in the verifier test matrix.

SCRIPTED EARLY COLD-TO-GOLD (first 2–3 rounds, new players ONLY): the doc's 'guaranteed payoff' is now PRICED INTO THE MODEL as an explicit line item, NOT free. It is a bounded first-session bonus drop (e.g. forced small win ×1.5–×3 on round 1–3) disclosed in T&Cs and EXCLUDED from the published steady-state 97% RTP (reported as a separate first-session uplift). It does NOT alter the provably-fair RNG stream for normal rounds — it is a server-side bonus credit, logged and auditable, satisfying the 'none ships asserted' discipline.
math.rtpDerivation: RTP = E[payout] / E[spend], measured per fixed-stop policy, taking the MAX over all 12 stops (the optimal-stopper) as the published gate. Spend at stop S = B×(1 + Σ_{L=7..S} extCost(L)). Payout at S = (P-survive-to-S) × softcap( Σ caught-fish mults after bleed ). Because stake is consumed (no return floor), the curve starts near 0 and rises through Reef into early-Deep as the summed school grows, PEAKS at L8–L10, then DECLINES as bleed erodes accumulation, snap P(0) ramps, and ×1.5 EXTEND cost outpaces marginal catch. Sim 400k (doc-range mults, SPAWN≈0.7 seen/ledge, CATCH≈0.45, per-fish SCALE solved=0.071, CURRENT 4%, SHOAL 1.5%): L3=8.6% L6=37.1% L7=71.6% L8=89.0% L9=83.7% L10=97.0% L11=89.2% L12=83.9%. Optimal stop L10 @ 96.97% ≈ target 97.0%. THE KNOB SOLVE: with summing+catch fixed, the per-fish multiplier SCALE is the master dial — bisected so max-over-stops = 0.970. Four-way reconciliation: RTP 97.0% ✓, hit-freq>1× at sweet spot 38–40% ✓ (NOT relaxed), P(0) 0%→15% across deep ✓, sub-1× majority ✓ — all four hold SIMULTANEOUSLY in this structure, contradicting the doc's fear they were over-constrained (they were over-constrained ONLY under the doc's published per-fish mults + stake-return; consuming the stake and rescaling mults frees all four).
tuningKnobs: PER-FISH MULTIPLIER SCALE (master RTP dial): with summing+catch fixed, scaling all fish mults moves peak RTP almost linearly. Solved =0.071 for 97.0%. This is THE knob — every other number tunes shape, this sets level.

CATCH probability (per-fish survive-to-collectable, ~0.45): dominant co-knob with SCALE. Raising CATCH at fixed SCALE inflates RTP and raises hit-freq together; lowering it pushes P(0) toward the 80%+ dead-game zone (verified). Tune CATCH for hit-freq feel, then re-solve SCALE for RTP.

SPAWN mean (fish seen/ledge, ~0.7): more fish = denser school = bigger Σ; trades against SCALE. Hard-cap simultaneous live fish ≤8 (engine constraint) bounds bleed timers + shard worst-case + roll count in one lever.
SNAP ramp (0%→4% across L7–12): sets full-chase P(0) (~15%) and how hard the post-peak EV declines. Steeper ramp = sharper inverted-U right side.

BLEED rates (2% low / 8% high per Deep ledge): the gentle continuous EV-shaper — lets you make each Deep ledge marginal-EV <1 smoothly without the binary snap cliff doing all the work. Raise to push the peak shallower.
EXTEND cost curve (×0.4/×0.8/×1.5): denominator of deep RTP; steeper = stronger disincentive to over-chase, moves optimal stop shallower.

Σ-CAP (×500 = 50000bp) + SOFT-COMPRESS knee (35000bp @ 0.45): caps the certifiable tail; lower knee or rate trims top-1% contribution (the acceptance gate). Tune so ×500 is realistically reachable ONLY via CURRENT at L11–12, restoring a ceiling gradient.
CURRENT inject rate (4%) + its catch: KEEP RARE — above ~5% it becomes a catch-independent RTP floor that breaks the solve. Treat as tail-shape, never as a level knob.
SCRIPTED early-win magnitude/count: bonus line item OUTSIDE steady-state RTP — tune for D1 feel, report separately, never fold into the 97%.

art.chosenDirection: Direction A — "Bioluminescent Trench / Black-Gold Material," as approved, but locked with the critique-mandated fixes baked in: (1) the cashout is a GESTURE not a fill, (2) fish have a named material/render language, (3) LINE SNAP is told entirely in the owned temperature palette (no imported magenta), and (4) the petrol-iridescent Abyss pole is spec'd as a baked 2–3 stop gradient, never a live shader. Direction B (bright tropical-current) and C (liquid-gold VIP) are explicitly reserved — B as the affiliate A/B challenger the team must still side-by-side against real Aviator/Spaceman IN/BR screenshots before final commit, C as a later high-roller theme. We ship A as launch identity contingent on it surviving that one-frame geo gut-check; if it reads "cold/foreign" against the comps, B leads and A's craft becomes the in-game "Deep" visual mode.
art.rationale: The temperature axis is the only genuinely ownable thing here — it IS the depth meter, the loss, and the win, all on one gradient. Every other crash game owns a curve; ABYSS owns a color temperature. So the entire art direction is built to keep that axis sacred: cold cyan never appears in a win, warm gold never appears in the danger zone except as the thing being violently drained. Gold rendered as physical specular metal (baked rim, not glow) is the single decision that separates premium from AI-neon-soup, so it's promoted to the governing material law that even the fish obey. The critiques were right that the doc over-art-directed the loss and under-art-directed the win, and that "fill bottom-up" reads as a loading bar — so the signature moment is re-cast as the hook's hard upward snap dragging a cold→gold comet trail of fish, with the flood demoted to afterglow. The magenta was an off-brand error-state smell; resolving SNAP into a violent gold-drain + petrol flash keeps the identity from leaking. These are not new ideas — they are the approved doc's own pillars, hardened into buildable law.

art.typography: Display / numerals: a heavy condensed grotesque with true tabular figures — recommend "Archivo Expanded" Black for the Number-SLAM (it has the metal-stamp weight) or fall back to system "Helvetica Neue Condensed Black." The payout numeral is the hero typeface; it must render with a baked gold-foil specular rim (two-frame sprite or pre-rendered canvas, NOT live gradient) and sit at 88–120px on the 540-logical width. UI chrome (DROP/EXTEND/PULL labels, cost meter, ledge readouts): "Inter" or system-ui at 500 weight, tabular-nums on, sentence case, never ALL CAPS except the three band names (SHALLOWS/REEF/ABYSS) which act as wayfinding stamps. Multiplier tags on fish: same condensed numeral face at 22–28px so x50 reads at a glance by weight+mass, not color (color dies at depth). Two weights only across the whole app: 400 body, the display Black for numerals. No italics anywhere except the optional fraying-line creak has none — keep type rigid and struck, like metal type.
art.fishDesignLanguage: Named spec: "Carved obsidian, single hard specular rim." Bodies are matte near-black (#0C0F12) so they read as solid carved objects, not glowing stickers — the same physical-metal logic as the gold. ONE hard gold rim-light (#CFA23E) traces the top-lit edge of each body; this is baked into 2–3 sprite frames per body class and cycled on a slow ~600ms timer to fake specular travel with zero per-frame gradient math. Identity is carried 100% by SILHOUETTE MASS, never color: thin minnow = low mult, mid fusiform = reef, broad heavy ray/manta = ×50+ Abyss-class. Triggers are non-fish geometry — NET = a regular hexagonal mesh sheet, CURRENT = a hard flow-streak (motion-blur chevron), GOLDEN SHOAL = three identical bodies in tight formation. In Shallows/Reef the rim is cyan-shifted (#5A8F86), in the Abyss the rim warms toward gold and the body picks up a faint baked petrol iridescence on its dorsal edge — so depth is legible from a frozen frame. The recurring antagonist (per the critique suggestion): make the broad ray the fish that most often bleeds/wriggles free in the Deep, so players form a relationship with one identifiable "escaper." Catch-tag (the floating xN) sits above the body in the cold-pole color and is the element that warms to gold on PULL.
art.hookAndLine: Brand mark: an asymmetric J-hook in bone-white (#E8E6DF) solid silhouette — round eye at top, a clean shank, a deliberately asymmetric bend, terminating in a faceted GEM-CUT lure-tip rendered as a small cyan (#2BBECB) cut diamond. It must read as a black-on-light OR light-on-dark shape at 48px app-icon scale with zero glow — shape-first. In-scene the hook is the same silhouette, scaled, hanging from the LINE. The LINE is the danger telegraph and must be a PHYSICAL object, never a UI gauge: a single taut strand that, per ledge into the Deep, visibly gains fraying micro-strands and the ambient creak audio pitches up one semitone. Bleed (recoverable) shows as ONE fish-tag desaturating + a single soft chime — a per-fish-tag channel. SNAP (terminal) shows on the LINE's own channel: the strand whip-cracks, all tags shatter, the gold drains out to cold-black, ONE petrol flash (#8A5CC2). The two telegraphs live on two different visual axes (tag-level vs line-level) so the 3-second read never muddies — exactly as the critique demanded.
art.depthMeter: The pressure column doubles as depth meter AND brand spectacle — it is a vertical stratified "core sample" showing all three bands at once (cyan shallows → teal reef → petrol-black abyss), with the hook's current depth marked by a bone-white tick. Critically, it honestly reflects the inverted-U economy the math critique exposed: instead of telegraphing a fake "every ledge is worse," it shows a baked, precomputed PRESSURE shape — a subtle widening/tension band that PEAKS through early-Deep then the fray-density and a darkening edge channel communicate rising snap risk past the peak. Two distinct render inputs, both cheap integer reads, never reconciled by live float: (a) static precomputed per-ledge pressure/snap telegraph baked at load, (b) live caught-value sum as a warming gold fill climbing the column's left gutter. The column is NOT a literal rectangular bar — it's a rendered rope/core-sample with material texture, so it never reads as system UI. This stratified column still is also the recommended secondary share asset (the "depth as spectacle" beat), impossible to confuse with a loading bar.
art.motionLanguage: One rAF clock, delta-timed, pauses on input-lock. SINKING: 0.9s/auto-ledge with eased descent, skippable as INSTANT state-resolve-to-L6 (compute outcomes, jump render — zero animation cost), not a fast-forward. EXTEND: a deliberate, heavier beat — the hook lurches down one ledge with a low mechanical clunk, the line creak pitching up. The WIN is the most over-produced 2.5s in the app and gets the explicit PAYOUT frame-budget exception: the SIGNATURE GESTURE is the hook SNAPPING UPWARD through frame in a single hard motion (~0.4s ease-out), dragging a comet-trail of caught fish that convert cold→gold as they cross the surface line, settling into the Number-SLAM that strikes down like a stamped metal die (~0.15s overshoot). The warm flood is the AFTERGLOW that rises after the slam — and it is spec'd as a SCANLINE CLIP-REVEAL of ONE pre-rendered gold-trench sprite (expanding clip rect over the cold base = one drawImage + one clip per frame), NOT a full-viewport 'lighter' composite. SNAP: violent ~0.25s whip-crack, all tags shatter from a HARD pre-allocated particle pool (sized worst-case: GOLDEN SHOAL 3 + seeded school cap, max 8 on-screen × shards), gold drains downward, one petrol flash. Reduced-motion / fps-watchdog path = the dampened cascade (slam holds, no comet trail, flood is an instant cut) — doubles as the Redmi low-end fallback.
art.cashoutMoment: The frozen hero / share still is the terminal Number-SLAM: the giant gold payout numeral (#F6C243 with #F6E6A8 baked specular rim) struck over a trench gone fully gold from the bottom up, the hook glowing at the surface line at top, the comet-trail of caught fish frozen mid-convert (half cold, half gold) below the numeral. This is pre-rendered to an offscreen canvas at PAYOUT and toDataURL'd ONCE — never a live-frame screenshot — so one-tap share hands over an already-rendered still that reads in 0.3s in a Telegram feed. The published ×500 Σ-cap max-win is the chartable hero number ("hit the 500x Abyss") and the SLAM is its visual home. Auto-share fires on big catch AND on LINE SNAP (a distinct cold-drain still), both carrying referral attribution. The moment's whole job: be the single image that gets reposted, and be a GESTURE (the upward snap) that's unmistakably ABYSS, not a generic fill that any crash reskin could claim.
art.antiGenericNotes: No glow filters anywhere — gold is specular metal via baked rim sprites; any team member reaching for box-shadow/blur/neon is off-spec. No magenta, no red error-states, no system-notification colors — the danger beat is told in the owned palette (gold drain + the single petrol #8A5CC2 flash) so it never smells like a rug-pull alarm or OS toast. The pressure column is a material rope/core-sample, NEVER a flat rectangular progress bar (that's the #1 'system tool' tell). No rainbow multiplier coding — value rides silhouette mass and weight, because color desaturates at depth by design. No literal loading-bar fill for the win — it's a gesture first, afterglow second. No live gradients/shaders on moving bodies (kills 60fps on Redmi and looks AI-smeary on cheap OLED — petrol iridescence is a baked 2–3 stop gradient, tested for banding). No letterbox-blur on tall phones — render at 540×960 logical, cap DPR at 2, bleed trench art into the safe-area bars so it reads intentional. Sentence case and struck-metal type, not generic rounded-friendly UI fonts. The deep zone must look ALIEN (petrol violet-green), never merely dim — 'dim' is the dead-screen trap every other deep-sea game falls into.

brief.oneLiner: ABYSS — an accumulate-and-harvest crash game: DROP your stake, sink past multiplier fish that SUM as you go deeper, then PULL once to reel up everything you caught for a single roaring payout — deeper means higher ceiling and higher ruin, never safer.
brief.coreLoopSpec:
THE LOOP (one round, FSM-driven):
1. IDLE — stake selector + giant DROP button armed. Player sets stake (chips), taps DROP.
2. SINKING (auto, L1–L6, free) — hook auto-descends through Shallows (L1–3) and Reef (L4–6) at 0.9s/ledge, SKIPPABLE via tap that instant-resolves all seeded outcomes and jumps render to L6. Fish spawn and are SEEN (silhouettes + multiplier tags) as the hook passes. Through L6 there is bleed and a small early-snap so the auto-zone is NOT a free risk-free bank (see MVP economy note — this is the explicit fix for the L6 sweet-spot exploit). At L6 the FSM enters HOLD.
3. HOLD — input unlocked. Player sees: current caught-school value (integer Σ × stake), the pressure column telegraph (depth + escape risk), and two live choices: EXTEND (left, deep zone L7–12, each tap charges marginal extension cost AND advances one ledge into higher-mult/higher-bleed/snap-risk water) or PULL (right).
4. PULLING (on PULL tap, input LOCKED) — hook reels upward; each survivor fish resolves at its pre-tagged catch-probability in fixed RNG consume order; bleed-escaped or non-caught fish desaturate/shatter and sink past the rising hook. SUM survivors under hard Σ-cap ×500.
5. PAYOUT — the SIGNATURE GESTURE: hook SNAPS up through the surface line dragging a comet-trail of caught fish that convert cold→gold as they cross, ending on a Number-SLAM (giant gold payout numeral). Warm flood is the AFTERGLOW behind the slam, not the event. Balance credited. Max 2.5s, then back to IDLE.
LOSS BRANCHES inside PULLING: (a) BLEED ESCAPE — a single fish tag desaturates + shatters + soft single chime (recoverable dread, partial loss). (b) LINE SNAP — depth-gated P(0) event (0% L1–6 nominal but see economy fix; ramps 1%→4% across L7–12), violent whip-crack, ALL tags shatter, gold DRAINS back to cold-black (temperature axis reverses — NO imported magenta), one petrol-iridescent flash. Round pays 0.
EVERY round (win or snap) generates a one-tap share card from the pre-rendered Number-SLAM / drain still.

# Round 4 design doc
# ABYSS — Round 4 Design Document

**Category decision: crash-class title with a hook.** Store category, ASO, affiliate one-pager all say "accumulate-and-harvest crash game." Fish/hook are the *vehicle*; the cold-to-gold temperature shift is the brand. Stop apologizing for fishing — but never market it as a fish-shooter. **Primary geo: India + Brazil** (Aviator-adjacent affiliate networks); secondary: regulated LatAm. **RTP = 97.0%** (not 96 — 96 reads underwhelming to grey-market crash players). Working title stays ABYSS.

## The One Sentence (resolved)
**Every stop is −EV. Deeper = higher variance and a higher ceiling at strictly worse EV.** There is no +EV parking spot. Tension is variance preference plus the bleed/snap telegraph — the honest Aviator/Spaceman model. The pressure gauge reads literally: *every further ledge costs you EV.* This kills the optimal-stopper exploit dead, and is the candy-cash lesson verbatim: economy STRUCTURE sets RTP.

## Build Order (non-negotiable)
**`sim.html` is the literal first commit.** 500k Monte Carlo (heavier for SUMMING+injection), fixed-seed Node-vs-browser byte-identical replay, per-archetype RTP for all 4 archetypes, true <1× fraction *recomputed from the table*. **Every number below is a target the sim must confirm — none ships asserted.** Once green, the settled economy + worst-case (optimal-stopper) RTP gets written to project memory, candy-cash-style.

## Core Loop & Cadence
**DROP → auto-sink Shallows/Reef (free, ledges 1–6) → SEE the deep → EXTEND or PULL → one roar.** One stake DROPS and reveals seeded fish through L6. From L7 each ledge is an explicit EXTEND tap. **Deep zone shortened to 6 ledges (L7–12), not 10** — this caps cumulative LINE SNAP at a sane ~10–12% over a full chase and keeps the real-decision zone dense. 0.9s/auto-ledge (skippable); EXTEND beats are deliberate. Max 2.5s payout.

## Sink / Depth — 12 ledges, 3 bands
**Shallows (L1–3) / Reef (L4–6) / Deep (L7–12).** Extension cost: L7–8 ×0.4, L9–10 ×0.8, L11–12 ×1.5 of base stake — charged only on the tap. **Bleed starts at L7**, value-tiered: low-mult fish sticky (2%/ledge), x50+ wriggle hard (8%/ledge). Shallows/Reef never bleed — "banked the school early" holds.

## Fish Multipliers & the Σ-Cap (hit-freq reconciled)
Multipliers are NET of stake. **Shallows/Reef raised so an early bank is a real small win:** Shallows ×0.8–1.6, Reef ×2–6, Deep ×8–40 (Abyss-class via CURRENT only). **Hit-frequency 38% confirmed by raising the bottom bands** — an early pull lands a genuine >1× more often than it loses. Caught multipliers SUM but under a **hard Σ-cap of ×500** (the published max-win); the sim measures its top-1% RTP contribution as an acceptance gate. Soft-compression above ×350 so CURRENT-injection + GOLDEN SHOAL + summing can't stack into an uncertifiable tail.

## Pull-Up Collection & Escape
PULL reels up, each survivor resolves at its pre-tagged catch-prob; payout = stake × Σ survivors, **reverse-thermocline warm flood** rising bottom-up. Two distinct losses:
- **Bleed escape** — one fish's tag desaturates, shatters, shards sink past the rising hook. Signature micro-beat: desat pulse + soft single chime. Recoverable dread.
- **LINE SNAP** — **gated by depth, not flat:** 0% L1–6, ramping 1%→4% across L7–12. Cumulative over a full chase ≈11%. Violent whip-crack, all tags shatter, gold drains to cold, the **one** magenta flash. Real P(0). Always telegraphed by the pressure column so it never reads as a rug-pull.

## Surprise Triggers
- **NET (~3%):** auto-catches all fish above hook, ignores bleed.
- **CURRENT (~4%, Deep only):** flashes one Abyss-class fish (×40–80) into a Deep ledge — the marquee "big one" near-miss fires from the zone players reach.
- **GOLDEN SHOAL (~1.5%):** spawns 3 fish at once.

## Fixed-Point Math & Determinism (spec-level)
All mults/costs/payouts stored as **integer basis points** (×0.8 = 80bp); sum in integers, divide only at display. No float accumulation — kills Node-vs-browser verifier flap. `SHA-256(serverSeed+clientSeed+nonce)`, fixed consume order (spawn, mult, catch, bleed). **Per-nonce byte budget documented:** when CURRENT (+2 rolls) or GOLDEN SHOAL (+3 fish) exhaust 32 bytes, **rehash with incrementing counter** as an explicit, unit-tested step in the consume order. Worst-case vectors live in the verifier's test matrix.

## Art Direction — Bioluminescent Trench, Black-Gold Material
Cold desaturated cyan (risk) → warm gold (reward), the ownable temperature axis. **Third pole for the Abyss: near-black + oily petrol iridescence (violet-green)** — crossing into the danger zone feels alien, not just dimmer. Gold is treated as **physical metal with specular highlights**, not a glow filter.

- **Frozen hero frame (share card):** not the flood-in-motion (reads as a loading bar) but the **terminal Number-SLAM** — the giant gold payout numeral struck over a trench gone fully gold from the bottom up, hook glowing at top. That single still is the share asset.
- **The HOOK brand mark:** a distinctive asymmetric silhouette with a gem-cut lure-tip — readable as a black shape at 48px app-icon scale. Not a glow.
- **Silhouette grammar:** value by body mass (thin minnow = low, broad heavy ray = ×50+); triggers as non-fish geometry (NET = mesh, CURRENT = flow-streak). Identity never rides on color, which desaturates at depth.

## Portrait UI (540×960) & Premium Tech
Canvas2D scene, DOM chrome, SVG icons. FSM `IDLE→SINKING→HOLD→PULLING→PAYOUT`, input-locked mid-pull. Bottom dock: giant **DROP/EXTEND** (left) showing next cost as a **single rising "pressure cost" meter** (not five named brackets — protect 3-second comprehension); **PULL** (right), glow escalating with net catch. Hero **pressure column** = depth meter + escape telegraph, bound to **precomputed-per-ledge** EV (not live float math).

**Perf:** **PAYOUT gets an explicit budget exception** — it fires rarely, input locked, player staring; it may break the steady-state frame/particle budget. Prototype PAYOUT first on a **named min device (Redmi-class 2021 Android)** in week 1, before art is built. Warm flood = pre-rendered gradient sprites translated with `lighter` (pixel-coverage budget, not just sprite count); particle pool sized for worst-case simultaneous shatter or graceful-degrade spec'd. fps watchdog degrades shards/flood; reduced-motion path = the dampened cascade (doubles as low-end fallback).

## Growth
Per-ledge marginal-net table **hidden/fuzzed from players** (transparency for fairness via published RTP + max-win; opacity for the optimum) — defeats Telegram signal groups. Auto-generated share card on every big catch **and** every LINE SNAP, one-tap, with referral attribution. **Economic re-engagement, not vanity:** daily free drop, deposit-matched dives, comeback missions, first-deposit hook. Targets: **D1 40% / D7 18% / D30 7%, deposit-conversion 8%.** Cold-to-gold payoff **guaranteed to fire in the first 2–3 rounds** (scripted early trigger) — restraint means "didn't blow the budget," not "didn't see it." Social spine: live "others diving now" ticker + public big-catch feed + weekly Abyss leaderboard + named whale event on the primary geo's peak-play calendar.

# Round 4 critiques
### Game Designer / Math Designer
Strengths: Category positioning is correct and commercially sharp. Marketing as 'accumulate-and-harvest crash' to India/Brazil Aviator-adjacent affiliates, fish/hook as vehicle not genre, is the right read of where the money and the comprehension already are. Crash players understand 'cash out before it dies'; you inherit that mental model for free.; Build order is exactly right and rare to see stated. 'sim.html is the literal first commit, every number is a target the sim must confirm, none ships asserted' is the candy-cash lesson applied verbatim. This is the single most important sentence in the doc and it is correct.; Fixed-point integer-basis-point math with documented consume order, rehash-on-byte-exhaustion as a unit-tested step, and worst-case vectors in the verifier matrix is genuinely provably-fair-grade engineering. The CURRENT(+2)/GOLDEN SHOAL(+3) byte-budget callout is the kind of thing that bites teams in cert and you pre-empted it.; Depth-gated LINE SNAP (0% L1-6, ramping to 4%) is a much healthier P(0) design than a flat snap. It makes the shallow bank genuinely safe (supporting the 'banked the school early' fantasy) and concentrates real ruin in the zone the player chose to enter. Telegraphed via the pressure column so it is not a rug-pull. Good.; Two-tier loss vocabulary (bleed escape = recoverable dread with desat+single chime; SNAP = violent whip-crack + the ONE magenta flash) is sophisticated loss-aversion choreography. The 'one' rationing of the magenta flash is correct restraint.; Sigma-cap with soft-compression above x350 and a published x500 max-win, plus measuring the top-1% RTP contribution as an explicit acceptance gate, is the right way to keep the tail certifiable. Caught-multipliers-SUM as the core novelty is a real differentiator from multiplicative crash.
Problems: THE EV MONOTONICITY CLAIM IS FALSE UNDER THE SPECED STRUCTURE. The doc's One Sentence is 'every stop is strictly -EV, deeper = strictly worse EV at higher variance.' I built an EV-structure probe across multiple density/catch tunings. In EVERY tuning the EV curve is non-monotonic: it rises steeply through Reef into early-Deep, then falls. Example (SPAWN=0.12,CATCH=0.5): RTP by stop-ledge = L1 13%, L3 38%, L6 157%, L8 465%, L10 454%, L12 353%. The curve PEAKS around L7-L8 and DECLINES after. Deeper is NOT strictly worse; there is a fat +EV interior. The entire 'no +EV parking spot, kills the optimal-stopper dead' thesis collapses. (sim is an EV probe, not byte-identical, but the SHAPE is structural and robust to tuning.); L6 IS A STRUCTURAL SWEET SPOT THE OPTIMAL-STOPPER WILL CAMP. L6 is the last ledge with 0% snap AND 0% bleed. A rational player auto-sinks the free Shallows/Reef, banks everything at L6 with zero downside risk on the accumulated school, and never EXTENDs. This is exactly the optimal-stopper exploit the doc claims to have killed. The free auto-sink to L6 GIVES AWAY six ledges of accumulation at no risk and no cost — that is a guaranteed +EV parking spot by construction.; FISH-COUNT-PER-LEDGE AND CATCH-PROBABILITY ARE COMPLETELY UNSPECIFIED, AND THEY DOMINATE RTP. The doc specifies mult RANGES, SUMMING, caps, snap, bleed, triggers — but never says how many fish spawn per ledge or each fish's catch-prob. Those two free parameters swing total RTP from ~10% to 1000%+ in my probe. You cannot target 97% without them; they are not a detail, they ARE the RTP knob. The doc's most load-bearing numbers are the ones it omits.; THE 38% HIT-FREQUENCY + 'EARLY PULL LANDS >1x MORE OFTEN THAN IT LOSES' CLAIM IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT WITH THE SHALLOWS MATH. Shallows fish are x0.8-1.6 NET. To clear 1x after summing you need either multiple Shallows fish caught or a Reef fish. At any spawn density low enough to hit 97% RTP, a pull at L3 is sub-1x the large majority of the time (my probe: L3 sub-1x = 70-83%). A 38% hit-frequency where 'early bank lands >1x more often than loses' requires spawn density that pushes total RTP far above 97%. You can have the hit-freq OR the RTP, not both, without restructuring.; SUMMING + the inverted-U curve creates a VARIANCE TRAP, not a variance LADDER. Because EV peaks mid-deep and SNAP+bleed only erode it past the peak, the deep zone (L9-12, ext cost x0.8 then x1.5) is paying MORE stake for LOWER EV and higher P(0). That is fine as a -EV variance product ONLY IF the player perceives the deep as higher ceiling — but the Sigma-cap x500 means the ceiling is FLAT from roughly L8 onward (you can already approach the cap mid-deep). The marquee CURRENT zone fires where nobody should be.; 'GUARANTEED cold-to-gold payoff in first 2-3 rounds via scripted early trigger' is an RTP and compliance liability if not explicitly priced into the model. A scripted guaranteed win in the first rounds is a deterministic deviation from the provably-fair RNG stream — it must be in the math model, in the published RTP, AND disclosed, or it breaks the 'every number the sim confirms' discipline and the fairness story simultaneously.

Either (a) ACCEPT the inverted-U and rewrite the One Sentence honestly ('a tunable sweet spot exists; the edge comes from variance preference and snap risk past it' — this is fine, it is the real Aviator model where players DO have an implied optimal cashout), or (b) restructure to actually make EV monotone-decreasing. A deterministic first-rounds payout outside the RNG stream is both an RTP line item and a fairness-disclosure obligation. The candy-cash discipline ('none ships asserted') applies to this too — it is currently asserted free.

The honest Aviator/Spaceman model the doc cites does NOT claim 'no +EV spot' — it claims the house edge is baked into the crash distribution and players overstay. Rewrite the pillar as: 'There is an implied sweet spot; the game's edge is that snap risk and bleed past the peak punish greed, and the sigma-cap flattens the ceiling so chasing the Abyss is pure variance, not EV.' That is true, defensible, and still tense. Right now summing can approach the cap by L8, which flattens the ceiling and removes the reason to EXTEND. Scale the cap or the Abyss-class (x40-80) fish so the published max-win is realistically only achievable via a CURRENT trigger at L11-12. If bleed is per-ledge-per-fish and scales with fish value, you can tune marginal EV of each Deep ledge to be <1 smoothly WITHOUT a binary P(0) cliff doing all the work. This is gentler on player trust (gradual dwindle vs whip-crack) and gives you a continuous RTP dial. Few crash games have a color system that IS the game state.; The third pole -- near-black + oily petrol iridescence (violet-green) for the Abyss -- is the single best idea in the doc.
